definitions.explanation: The state of being unable to make a decision, going back and forth without taking action. Often implies reluctance to move forward due to uncertainty or doubt.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{一瞬|いっしゅん}の{逡巡|しゅんじゅん}の{後|あと}、{決断|けつだん}した。
examples.english: After a moment's hesitation, he made his decision.

examples.japanese: {転職|てんしょく}について{逡巡|しゅんじゅん}している。
{逡巡|しゅんじゅん}している{場合|ばあい}ではない。
examples.english: This is no time to hesitate.

notes:
KANJI BREAKDOWN:
・{逡|しゅん} - to hesitate, to retreat
・{巡|じゅん} - to go around, to patrol

The compound captures the idea of going back and forth, retreating and circling without progressing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{逡巡|しゅんじゅん}する - to hesitate, to waver
・{逡巡|しゅんじゅん}の{末|すえ} - after much hesitation
・{逡巡|しゅんじゅん}の{色|いろ}を{見|み}せる - to show signs of hesitation
・{逡巡|しゅんじゅん}なく - without hesitation

USAGE:
Somewhat literary and formal. Used in:
・{小説|しょうせつ} - novels
・{記事|きじ} - articles
・Formal speech

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
・{躊躇|ちゅうちょ} - hesitation (more common)
・{迷|まよ}い - doubt, wavering
・ためらい - hesitation
・{優柔不断|ゆうじゅうふだん} - indecisiveness

NUANCE:
{逡巡|しゅんじゅん} has a slightly more literary tone than {躊躇|ちゅうちょ} and suggests prolonged hesitation with internal conflict.

REGISTER:
Slightly formal/literary. Common in written Japanese and formal discussions.
